content.title: Can GameStop’s Silent Hill Tie-In Reveal the Real Potential of Its Experiential Strategy (GME)?
content.summary: Cineverse announced that it partnered with GameStop Corp. on an immersive, in-store and theatrical marketing campaign for the film Return to Silent Hill, running at selected GameStop locations near cinemas ahead of the movie’s January 23 wide U.S. release. The collaboration links GameStop’s physical stores with a film based on the Silent Hill 2 video game, underscoring how the retailer is testing experiential, cross-channel engagement to reach gaming and horror fans. content.title: 1 Internet Stock on Our Watchlist and 2 We Turn Down
content.summary: Consumer internet businesses are redefining how people engage with the world by giving them instant connectivity and convenience. This influence cuts both ways though because they have high exposure to the ups and downs of consumer spending, and the market seems to believe the tide is turning in the wrong direction - over the past six months, the industry has tumbled by 1.9%. This performance is a noticeable divergence from the S&P 500’s 10% return.

content.summary: 99% That's how much value AMC Entertainment has lost from a peak hit in January 2021, during an eruption of meme-stock mania that swept up GameStop, BlackBerry and others. 📉 I dig into why speculators keep dabbling in meme stocks, despite mostly awful returns, in the latest edition of my Markets A.

content.title: Why Meme Stocks Still Matter
content.summary: The original squeeze, and Keith Gill’s (aka Roaring Kitty’s) rise to fame, was painted as a David versus Goliath battle because a huge hedge fund was humbled.  Author Kyla Scanlon had a fascinating take on why young people are especially engaged in a Journal guest article last month: It’s “financial nihilism,” she says.
